# Judith Chapter 5 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 5 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_005_page_001.jpg

---

**1** Holofernes, the chief commander of the Assyrian forces, was informed that the Israelites had prepared for war, had blocked the mountain passes, had fortified all the peaks of the high hills, and had placed obstacles in the plains.

**2** He was furious beyond measure. He summoned all the rulers of Moab and the generals of Ammon and all the governors of the seacoast,

**3** and said to them: "Tell me, you sons of Canaan — who is this people that lives in the hill country? What cities do they inhabit? How large is their army? Where does their power and strength lie? Who has set himself up as their king and leads their forces?

**4** And why have they alone, of all who dwell in the west, refused to come out and meet me?"

**5** Then Achior, the commander of all the Ammonites, said to him: "Let my lord hear a word from the mouth of his servant, and I will tell you the truth about this people who live near you; no lie shall come from my mouth.

**6** This people is descended from the Chaldeans.

**7** They sojourned formerly in Mesopotamia, because they were unwilling to follow the gods of their fathers who were in the land of the Chaldeans.

**8** They abandoned the way of their fathers and worshiped the God of Heaven, the God whom they had come to know. Their fathers drove them out from before their gods, and they fled into Mesopotamia and sojourned there for many days.

**9** Then their God commanded them to depart from their dwelling place and journey to the land of Canaan. There they settled and were enriched with gold and silver and great numbers of livestock.

**10** When a famine spread over all the face of the land of Canaan, they went down to Egypt and sojourned there until they had grown great. There they became so numerous that their host could not be counted.

**11** So the king of Egypt rose up against them and outwitted them with forced labor and brick-making, humbled them and made them into slaves.

**12** They cried out to their God, and he struck the whole land of Egypt with plagues for which there was no remedy. The Egyptians drove them out from before them.

**13** Then God dried up the Red Sea before them,

**14** and led them by the way of Sinai and Kadesh-Barnea. They drove out all who inhabited the desert

**15** and settled in the land of the Amorites, utterly destroying by their own strength all who dwelt in Heshbon. Then they crossed the Jordan and took possession of all the hill country.

**16** They drove out before them the Canaanites and Perizzites and Jebusites and Shechemites and all the Girgashites, and they lived there for many days.

**17** And so long as they did not sin against their God, they prospered, for a God who hates iniquity was with them.

**18** But when they strayed from the way he had appointed for them, they were devastated in many great battles and carried captive into a land that was not their own. The temple of their God was razed to the ground and their cities were seized by their enemies.

**19** But now they have turned back and returned to their God. They have come up from the places of dispersion where they were scattered, have taken possession of Jerusalem where their sanctuary is, and have settled in the hill country, for it had been left desolate.

**20** So now, my lord and master, if there is any offense in this people and they are sinning against their God — and if we can identify that stumbling block among them — then we should go up and fight against them.

**21** But if there is no iniquity among their nation, then let my lord pass them by, lest their Lord shield them and their God take their side, and we become a reproach before all the earth."

**22** When Achior had finished saying all this, the people standing around the tent began to murmur. The nobles of Holofernes and all those who lived by the sea and in Moab insisted that he should be cut down.

**23** "We are not afraid of the Israelites — they are a people with no strength and no capacity for a battle of any force.

**24** Let us advance, and they will become prey for the whole of your army to devour, Lord Holofernes."
